gaps.sentence: 'I didn't take your charger,' she insisted. She ___ taking my charger.
gaps.explanation: Denials are reported as deny + -ing: denied taking.

gaps.sentence: 'I work from home on Fridays,' he explained. He explained that he ___ from home on Fridays.
gaps.explanation: After a past reporting verb, present simple backshifts to past simple: work → worked.

gaps.sentence: 'Please, please don't leave me,' he sobbed. He begged her ___ leave him.
gaps.hint: beg sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: Negative begging: begged her not to leave; the negative precedes the infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll see you tomorrow,' he said. He said he would see me ___.
gaps.explanation: Time expressions shift: tomorrow becomes the next day / the following day.

gaps.sentence: 'She arrived last night,' he told us. He told us that she had arrived ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Last night' becomes the night before (the previous night) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw him this morning,' she said on Monday afternoon. She said she had seen him ___ morning.
gaps.explanation: This morning, reported later the same day, becomes that morning.

gaps.sentence: 'I don't like seafood,' he confessed. He confessed that he ___ like seafood.
gaps.explanation: Present simple negative backshifts: don't like → didn't like.

gaps.sentence: She ___ on seeing the manager immediately.
gaps.explanation: Only 'insist' takes on + -ing; suggest and offer take bare -ing/to-infinitive respectively.
